_role_in_the_gates: THE BLENDED COARSE ARM. Layered y+ 481.565. Its B2 comparator is DRIVAER-R2-COARSE-RERUN.
_B2_MUST_NOT_BE_SKIPPED: B1 ALONE CAN BE PASSED BY A NULL -- two meshes agreeing because the wall treatment never engaged reads as success. The registration's own words: 'If B2 shows no change, blending does nothing at y+ 481.6 and B1's agreement -- if it agrees -- means nothing. B2 is the limb that stops a null result being read as a pass.' B2 needs the non-blended run of the SAME mesh.
_CARRY_ACROSS_AN_INACTIVE_B2_IS_EXPECTED: AN INACTIVE B2 READING IS EXPECTED AND WOULD BE CORRECT PHYSICS, NOT A FAILED SWAP. The blended and log-law wall functions are numerically the SAME above y+ ~ 30 and differ only BELOW it: nut/nu agrees to 0.440 % at y+ 232.0 (medium layered) and 0.148 % at y+ 481.6 (coarse layered), because Spalding's law asymptotes to the log law at high y+. DrivAer's problem is y+ TOO HIGH, not too low. REGISTERED BEFORE THE ARMS RAN at DRIVAER_R2C_B2_INTERPRETATION_ADDENDUM.md (commits 99a49c026, 2ac8a35f6), with the local-equilibrium caveat that qualifies it: the two functions take DIFFERENT INPUTS (nutkWallFunction forms y+ from k; nutUSpaldingWallFunction solves for u_tau from U), so in a massively separated rear end where local equilibrium fails they can disagree regardless of y+. The asymptotic arithmetic is the prediction; the caveat is the named way it could be wrong.
